memory_lessons.applicability: Use the synchronous tiled program as the matched reference; preserve the same staging and compute mapping when testing pipeline depth.
memory_lessons.claim: The two-buffer cp.async candidate was valid and correct but measured slower than the synchronous 16×16 control, so correctness and asynchronous copying alone do not establish a speedup.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this three-slot, up-to-two-stage lookahead candidate for correctness and timing against the synchronous control and prior two-buffer result.

proposal.hypothesis: The prior two-buffer asynchronous candidate was correct but slower than the synchronous control. This contrasting three-slot ring prefetches up to two future K stages while retaining the 16×16 CTA, lane-to-data mapping, scalar FP32 compute mapping, and output operation. It tests whether deeper lookahead hides more copy latency, while its extra shared memory and buffer-reuse barrier may instead worsen performance; no gain is claimed before measurement.

retained: Retained the 16×16 CTA, (ty,tx) cooperative A/B staging map, scalar FP32 accumulation, and alpha/beta output expression.

Replaced two shared-memory stages with a three-slot ring and preloaded up to two future K stages using cp.async groups; wait_group keeps the current stage ready while allowing later groups to remain outstanding.
Added a CTA synchronization before reusing a ring slot, zero-filled invalid row, column, and K-tail entries, and kept a synchronous fallback for architectures below sm_80.
Preserved the run entry point, default-stream launch, input/output buffers, and absence of extra allocations.
